AUD01_hotline_welcome_and_clinic_schedul.text: Thank you for calling the Singapore Manufacturing Federation Grant Advisory Hotline. This is a recorded message. Our advisory officers are available Monday to Friday. 9 in the morning to 5.30 in the evening. We are closed on weekends and public holidays. If you leave a message outside these hours, an advisory officer will return your call within three working days. The Federation runs a free grant clinic on the second and fourth Wednesday of every month. At Alexandra Point, Block A. fourth floor, each grant clinic session runs for 90 minutes and is limited to 12 member companies. So early registration is advised. Grant clinics are open to all corporate members at no charge. Non-members may attend one session as a guest before joining. Please bring three items to your grant clinic appointment. 1. Your ACRA Business Profile dated within the last six months. 2. Your financial statements for the past three financial years. 3. Any vendor quotation you have already received. Even a draft one. Please note carefully. Our advisory officers can explain scheme criteria, but they cannot tell you whether your company will be approved. Only Enterprise Singapore. Workforce Singapore. Or the relevant participating financial institution can make that decision. Thank you for calling the Singapore Manufacturing Federation.

AUD02_advisory_briefing_commencement_rul.text: This is a short internal briefing on the single most common reason our members lose a grant. We call it the commencement rule. Here is the situation you will meet again and again. A member calls you. They are excited. They have found the machine they want. And the supplier has offered them a discount if they confirm this week. They ask you whether they should put down a deposit to hold the price. The answer is no. Not a deposit. Not a signature. Not a purchase order. Nothing at all. The moment a member pays any money to a supplier who is named in the application. Or signs any contractual agreement with that supplier. The project counts as having started. A project that has already started cannot be funded. There is no appeal on this point and there is no retrospective application. Two things trip members up here. First, they believe a refundable deposit is safe because they could get the money back. It is not safe. The test is whether payment was made. Not whether it could be reversed. Second, they believe signing is safe as long as no money has moved. That is also wrong. The signed contractual agreement is commencement on its own. So make this your very first question on every call. Before you talk about eligibility. Before you talk about support rates. Before anything else. Ask them plainly. Have you paid anything? Or signed anything? For this project yet? If the answer is yes. Stop. Do not help them prepare an application that cannot succeed. Escalate the case instead. And be honest with the member about where they stand.

AUD03_member_webinar_scheme_routing.text: In this part of the webinar I want to help you work out which scheme fits which project. Because members lose a lot of time applying under the wrong one. Start with a simple question. Is the thing you want to buy already sitting on a government approved list? If it is, you are almost certainly looking at the Productivity Solutions Grant. That is the fast path. You pick the solution from the catalog. You get a quotation from the approved vendor. And you apply. Support is up to 50% of the cost for local small and medium enterprises. If what you need is not on any list, because it has to be built or integrated specifically for your operation. Then you are looking at the Enterprise Development Grant instead. That one needs a written project proposal and it is assessed individually. It takes longer, typically 8 to 12 weeks. But it funds work that no catalog could ever cover. Now here is the case that catches people out. A member calls and says they want to replace an old air compressor. And they ask about automation funding under the Enterprise Development Grant. That is the wrong scheme. Replacing equipment with a similar unit that adds no new capability is excluded under automation. But if the new unit is more energy efficient, then the energy efficiency grant is exactly the right instrument. And the support rate there is considerably more generous. So do not ask yourself what you are buying. Ask yourself what policy objective your purchase serves, productivity, or new capability, or energy efficiency, or entering a new export market. The objective tells you the scheme. The object almost never does. One last warning. You cannot claim the same cost item under two schemes. If a piece of software is on the Productivity Solutions grant approved list, you cannot put that same cost into an Enterprise Development Grant application as well. Split the scope. Or choose one.

AUD04_hotline_scope_and_escalation.text: Before we connect you to an advisory officer, please note what this advisory service can and cannot do. We can explain the eligibility criteria of enterprise Singapore in workforce Singapore support. Skines, we can explain what costs each scheme supports and excludes. We can walk you through the business grant portal submission process and we can review your documents before you submit them. We cannot tell you that your company is eligible or that your application will be approved. Only the administering agency can decide that we cannot submit or manage an application on your behalf. Because third-party application and management is not permitted under these schemes, we cannot advise on tax matters, customs duties, or company structuring. We cannot help you present your financial position differently in order to pass an assessment. If you ask us something outside this scope, our officers will tell you plainly that they cannot help and where possible they will point you to the right agency instead. Please also understand that support rates, gaps and deadlines change and 2026 is an unusually busy year for scheme changes. Where our officer is not certain that a figure is current, they will say so and they will check the official page with you rather than quote a number from memory. A wrong figure is worse than no figure, because members make commitments on the strength of what we tell them. Finally, if your inquiry does not name a specific scheme or if we do not yet know your sector, your company size, or your ownership, our officer will ask you a few questions first those details change the answer materially. So please bear with us. Thank you, connecting you now.
